subject: ela
intro: In a good classroom discussion, everyone follows rules that make the conversation fair and respectful. These rules include: taking turns and not talking over others, listening carefully when someone else speaks, raising your hand or waiting for the right moment to speak, and building on what your classmates say — not just repeating your own ideas. Good discussions help everyone learn more together.

items.prompt:
A class is discussing the story 'The Tortoise and the Hare.' Read what each student does:
  Maya raises her hand and waits to be called on before speaking.
  Jake calls out his answer without waiting.
Which student is following the discussion rules?

steps: Discussion rules include: gaining the floor respectfully — this means waiting your turn before speaking.
Maya raised her hand and waited — she is gaining the floor respectfully.
Jake called out without waiting — he did not follow the agreed-upon rules.
Taking turns ensures everyone gets a chance to speak and be heard.
solution.answer: Maya is following the discussion rules. She raised her hand and waited to be called on, which is how students gain the floor respectfully.

items.prompt:
The class has been discussing their favorite seasons. Listen to what two students say:
  Priya: 'I love summer because we go to the beach.'
  Marcus: 'I agree with Priya, AND I also love summer because we get to eat ice cream outside.'
What does Marcus do that makes his response a good discussion contribution?

steps: Marcus begins by linking to what Priya said: 'I agree with Priya.'
He does not just repeat her idea — he adds his own new information about ice cream.
This is called building on others' talk: linking your comment to what someone else said.
Good discussion contributors listen carefully and then ADD to the conversation.
solution.answer: Marcus builds on Priya's idea by first agreeing with her and then adding new information. This is an example of linking his comment to what a classmate said.

items.prompt:
The teacher asks: 'Why do you think the wolf blew the houses down?' Three students respond:
  Ana: 'Because he was hungry.'
  Ben: 'He wanted to eat the pigs.'
  Chen: 'I think he was hungry too, and Ben's idea makes sense — he was trying to get to the pigs because he was really hungry.'
Which student best builds on the conversation?

steps: Ana gives her own idea: 'Because he was hungry.'
Ben adds a similar idea: 'He wanted to eat the pigs.'
Chen links both ideas together — she agrees with Ana AND references Ben's comment.
Chen explicitly connects her contribution to remarks from two classmates.
Building on others' talk means showing you listened and are connecting ideas.
solution.answer: Chen best builds on the conversation. She links her comment to both Ana and Ben's remarks, showing she listened carefully and is connecting ideas across the discussion.

items.prompt:
During a discussion, Lila says: 'I think dogs make better pets than cats.' She is not sure exactly why. What would be the best way for another student to respond?
A) 'You're wrong — cats are better.'
B) 'Can you tell us more about why you think dogs are better?'
C) Start talking about a different topic entirely.

steps: Option A is a disagreement but does not ask for clarification or add reasoning.
Option C changes the topic, which does not build on Lila's comment.
Option B asks Lila to explain more — this is asking for clarification and further explanation.
Asking 'can you tell us more' keeps the discussion on topic and helps everyone understand Lila's thinking better.
solution.answer: B) 'Can you tell us more about why you think dogs are better?' This asks for clarification and further explanation, which deepens the discussion.

items.prompt:
Two students are talking at the same time during a class discussion. Their teacher stops the class and reminds everyone of a rule. Which rule was being broken?
A) Listen to others carefully and speak one at a time
B) Only the teacher can speak
C) Never disagree with a classmate

steps: When two students talk at the same time, no one can be heard clearly.
One of the key discussion rules is: speak one at a time.
This rule ensures everyone can be heard and everyone feels listened to.
Option B is not a discussion rule — students are encouraged to speak.
Option C is not a rule — respectful disagreement is allowed in discussions.
solution.answer: A) Listen to others carefully and speak one at a time. Two students speaking simultaneously breaks this rule.

items.prompt:
Read this classroom scenario:
Teacher: 'What happened at the beginning of the story?'
Student 1 (Zoe): 'The girl found a magic key in her garden.'
Student 2 (Sam): 'I already said my idea last time and no one listened.'
Student 3 (Mia): 'I think that connects to what Zoe said — the key must be important because she found it right at the start.'
Which student best follows the rules for collaborative discussion?
items.hint: Look for the student who listens to what was said and then builds on it, rather than focusing on themselves.

steps: Zoe contributes a relevant answer — that is good.
Sam's comment focuses on himself and is off topic — not following discussion rules.
Mia links her comment to Zoe's idea: 'I think that connects to what Zoe said.' She builds on the conversation.
Mia demonstrates both listening carefully and linking her comments to a classmate's remarks.
solution.answer: Mia best follows the rules for collaborative discussion. She listened to Zoe and built on her idea by linking her comment to what Zoe said.

items.prompt:
A student wants to share an idea during class discussion. Two other students are still talking. What should he do?
A) Shout loudly to get attention
B) Wait for them to finish, then raise his hand
C) Get up and tap the teacher on the shoulder
items.hint: Think about the rule: gain the floor in a respectful way. What does 'respectful' look like?

steps: Gaining the floor respectfully means waiting for the right moment, not interrupting.
Shouting or interrupting physically are not respectful ways to gain the floor.
Waiting for others to finish and then raising a hand is the respectful approach.
This shows respect for the current speakers and follows agreed-upon discussion rules.
solution.answer: B) Wait for them to finish, then raise his hand. This is how students gain the floor respectfully during a discussion.

items.prompt:
A student says: 'Penguins live in Antarctica.' Another student wants to link her comment to this. Which response best builds on the first student's idea?
A) 'I like polar bears too.'
B) 'That is interesting — and I read that they huddle together to stay warm in the cold.'
C) 'Can we talk about something else?'
items.hint: Building on someone's idea means adding new information that connects to what they said.

steps: Option A switches to polar bears — it does not connect to the penguin comment.
Option C changes the topic entirely — not building on the conversation.
Option B starts with acknowledgment ('That is interesting') and adds NEW connected information about penguins.
This response links directly to the first student's comment and deepens the conversation.
solution.answer: B) 'That is interesting — and I read that they huddle together to stay warm in the cold.' This builds on the first student's idea by adding new, connected information.

items.prompt:
During a discussion about community helpers, a student says something confusing. The class is not sure what she means. What is the BEST thing for another student to do?
A) Move on to the next topic without asking about it
B) Ask the student to explain more: 'Can you tell us what you mean by that?'
C) Tell the student she is wrong
items.hint: One of the discussion rules is to ask for clarification when you do not understand something.

steps: Moving on ignores the confusion — the class misses out on understanding.
Telling someone they are wrong is not the same as asking for clarification.
Asking 'Can you tell us what you mean?' is asking for clarification and further explanation.
This keeps the conversation respectful and helps everyone understand better.
solution.answer: B) Ask the student to explain more: 'Can you tell us what you mean by that?' This is asking for clarification, which is a key discussion skill.

items.prompt:
A class is having a discussion. Student A has been speaking for a long time. Student B keeps trying to interrupt. Student C waits patiently and then raises her hand when Student A is done.
Which behavior shows the BEST discussion skills?
A) Student A's long speaking turn
B) Student B's interrupting
C) Student C's waiting and then raising her hand
items.hint: Think about the rules: take turns, listen to others, and speak one at a time.

steps: Student A is speaking too long — good discussions involve balanced participation.
Student B is interrupting — this breaks the 'speak one at a time' rule.
Student C waits for Student A to finish and raises her hand — she is gaining the floor respectfully.
Student C's behavior best follows the agreed-upon rules for discussions.
solution.answer: C) Student C's waiting and raising her hand. She gains the floor respectfully — waiting for others to finish and signaling she wants to contribute.
